items.zh: 云何順算數？謂或由以一為一算數，或由以二為一算數，順次展轉數至其十，名順算數。云何逆算數？謂即由前二種算數，逆次展轉從第十數，次九、次八、次七、次六、次五、次四、次三、次二、次數其一，名逆算數。若時行者，或以一為一算數為依，或以二為一算數為依，於順算數及逆算數已串修習，於其中間心無散亂。無散亂心善算數已，復應為說勝進算數。云何名為勝進算數？謂或依以一為一算數，或依以二為一算數，合二為一而算數之。若依以一為一而算數者，即入息、出息二合為一。若依以二為一而算數者，即入息、出息四合為一。如是展轉數乃至十。如是後後漸增，乃至以百為一而算數之。
items.en: What is forward counting? Whether by the one-for-one method or the two-as-one method, counting forward in sequence up to ten — this is forward counting. What is backward counting? By either of those same two methods, counting backward from ten — nine, eight … down to one — this is backward counting. … When a practitioner has thoroughly practised forward and backward counting, by either method, such that the mind remains free of distraction throughout, and has mastered counting without distraction, one should then be taught advancing counting. What is advancing counting? Whether based on the one-for-one or the two-as-one method, one now counts two units as a single count. … Continuing to increase in this way, one eventually counts a hundred breaths as a single count.

items.zh: 由此以百為一算數，漸次數之乃至其十。如是勤修數息念者，乃至十十數以為一，漸次數之乃至滿十。由此以十為一算數，於其中間心無散亂，齊此名為已串修習。

items.title: Section: Mastery of Counting — Beyond the Need to Count

items.zh: 又此勤修數息念者，若於中間其心散亂，復應退還從初數起，或順、或逆。若時算數極串習故，其心自然乘任運道，安住入息、出息所緣，無斷無間相續而轉。先於入息有能取轉，入息滅已，於息空位有能取轉；次於出息有能取轉，出息滅已，於息空位有能取轉。如是展轉相續流注，無動無搖，無散亂行，有愛樂轉。齊此名為過算數地，不應復數。唯於入息、出息所緣，令心安住。於入出息應正隨行、應審了達。於入出息及二中間，若轉、若還分位差別，皆善覺了。如是名為算數修習。又鈍根者，應為宣說如是息念算數修習。彼由此故，於散亂處，令心安住、令心愛樂。若異算數入出息念，彼心應為惛沈睡眠之所纏擾，或應彼心於外馳散。由正勤修數息念故，彼皆無有。
items.en: If, in the midst of diligently cultivating mindfulness of the breath, the mind becomes distracted, one should withdraw and begin counting again from the start, whether forward or backward. … When counting has been so thoroughly practised that the mind naturally rides an effortless path, abiding on the object of the in-breath and out-breath without break or interruption … flowing on continuously in this way, unmoved, unshaken, free of distraction, with a sense of genuine delight — at this point one has passed beyond the stage of counting, and should count no longer, but simply let the mind abide on the in-breath and out-breath as its object. … For a practitioner of dull faculties, this cultivation through counting should be taught, so that in the midst of distraction the mind may be made to abide, and made to delight in the practice. … Through correctly and diligently cultivating mindfulness of the breath in this way, these afflictions are altogether absent.

items.title: Section: Counting Closes Entirely; Aggregates Opens as Mode Two

items.zh: 若有利根，覺慧聰俊，不好乘此算數加行。若為宣說算數加行，亦能速疾無倒了達，然不愛樂。彼復於此入出息緣安住念已，若是處轉、若乃至轉、若如所轉、若時而轉，於此一切，由安住念，能正隨行，能正了達如是加行有如是相。於此加行若修、若習、若多修習為因緣故，起身輕安及心輕安，證一境性，於其所緣愛樂趣入。如是彼於算數息念善修習已，復於所取、能取二事，作意思惟，悟入諸蘊。云何悟入？謂於入息、出息及息所依身，作意思惟，悟入色蘊。於彼入息、出息能取念相應領納，作意思惟，悟入受蘊。即於彼念相應等了，作意思惟，悟入想蘊。即於彼念，若念相應思及慧等，作意思惟，悟入行蘊。若於彼念相應諸心、意、識，作意思惟，悟入識蘊。如是行者，於諸蘊中乃至多住，名已悟入。是名悟入諸蘊修習。
items.en: A sharp-facultied practitioner, being naturally clear and quick of mind, does not take pleasure in this counting practice. Even if taught it, such a person understands it swiftly and without error, yet finds no delight in it. … Through practising, repeating, and thoroughly cultivating this discipline, physical and mental pliancy arise, one-pointedness is realised, and the practitioner enters this object with genuine delight. … Once a practitioner has thoroughly cultivated mindfulness through counting, further attending to the object grasped and the mind that grasps it leads to realising the aggregates. Attending to the in-breath, the out-breath, and the body they depend on realises the aggregate of form. Attending to the sensation accompanying the mindfulness that grasps the breath realises the aggregate of feeling. Attending to the recognition accompanying that mindfulness realises the aggregate of perception. Attending to the intention and discernment accompanying that mindfulness realises the aggregate of formations. Attending to the mind, mentation, and consciousness accompanying that mindfulness realises the aggregate of consciousness. Dwelling extensively within this realisation of the aggregates — this is called having truly realised them. This is cultivation through realising the aggregates.

items.title: Section: Dependent Origination Opens as Mode Three

items.zh: 若時無倒，能見能知唯有諸蘊、唯有諸行、唯事、唯法。彼於爾時，能於諸行悟入緣起。云何悟入？謂觀行者，如是尋求：此入出息何依何緣？既尋求已，如實悟入：此入出息依身緣身、依心緣心。復更尋求：此身此心何依何緣？既尋求已，如實悟入：此身此心依緣命根。復更尋求：如是命根何依何緣？既尋求已，如實悟入：如是命根依緣先行。
items.en: When, without distortion, one can see and know only aggregates, only conditioned formations, only events, only phenomena — at that time one is able to realise dependent origination with respect to these formations. How does one realise it? The contemplative practitioner inquires: on what does this in-breath and out-breath depend, and what is its condition? Having inquired, one truly realises: this in-breath and out-breath depends on the body and is conditioned by the body, depends on the mind and is conditioned by the mind. One inquires further: on what do this body and this mind depend, and what is their condition? Having inquired, one truly realises: this body and this mind depend on and are conditioned by the life faculty. One inquires yet further: on what does this life faculty depend, and what is its condition? Having inquired, one truly realises: this life faculty depends on and is conditioned by prior karmic action.

blocks.text: Counting is a raft: once across, one leaves it. Then the breath becomes a gateway into insight.
Count up to ten, or back from ten to one. "Continuing to increase, one eventually counts a hundred breaths as a single count." Master Cháng Bǎi: usually one moves on long before a hundred.

"If the mind becomes distracted, withdraw and begin counting again from the start." When counting is so practised that "the mind naturally rides an effortless path", one no longer needs to count. Venerable Miào Jìng: this is "following the breath".
"A sharp-facultied practitioner, naturally clear and quick of mind, does not take pleasure in this counting practice." Such a person goes straight to insight.

"Attending to the in-breath, the out-breath, and the body they depend on realises the aggregate of form"; the feeling of the breath, feeling; recognising it, perception; the intention and wisdom involved, formations; the mind that knows it, consciousness.

"Seeing only aggregates, only formations, only events": one inquires what the breath depends on. "This body and this mind depend on the life faculty"; the life faculty on prior karma; prior karma on ignorance. Venerable Miào Jìng explains the life faculty as what keeps body and mind together.

quiz.q: How does one count backward, and who, according to Master Cháng Bǎi, should use it?
options: from ten down to one; for very scattered minds, since a different method gathers the mind
quiz.why: "By either of those same two methods, counting backward from ten — nine, eight … down to one." Master Cháng Bǎi: those whose minds are very scattered can count backward; a different way of counting gathers the mind more easily.

quiz.q: Advancing counting can reach a hundred as one. Where does Master Cháng Bǎi say most practitioners switch to following the breath?
quiz.why: "Continuing to increase in this way, one eventually counts a hundred breaths as a single count." Master Cháng Bǎi: usually after practising four-as-one one turns to following the breath, since most minds cannot be still enough to count that many before one.

quiz.q: If the mind becomes distracted while counting, what does the treatise say to do?
options: go back and start counting from the beginning, forward or backward
quiz.why: "If, in the midst of diligently cultivating mindfulness of the breath, the mind becomes distracted, one should withdraw and begin counting again from the start, whether forward or backward." Venerable Miào Jìng: drop the count and start again from one, from the beginning.

quiz.q: "At this point one has passed beyond counting and should count no more." How do the masters describe this stage?
options: Miào Jìng: no more one-two-three — this is "following the breath"; Cháng Bǎi: the mind flows onto the breath drop by drop, eager for sitting time
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: no longer keeping track of one, two, three … ten — this should be "following the breath." Master Cháng Bǎi: like water dripping, drop after drop with no gap, the mind flows onto the breath; one even looks forward to sitting time.

quiz.q: How does a sharp-facultied practitioner regard counting, and how does Master Cháng Bǎi distinguish 覺 from 慧?
options: clear and quick, does not enjoy counting; 覺 is innate wisdom from past lives, 慧 acquired through effort
quiz.why: "A sharp-facultied practitioner, being naturally clear and quick of mind, does not take pleasure in this counting practice." Master Cháng Bǎi: 覺 is wisdom cultivated in past lives, innate; 慧 is wisdom acquired by effort. The English merges them.

quiz.q: In realising the aggregates, attending to what realises the form aggregate, and is this calm or insight, according to Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: the in-breath, out-breath, and the body they rely on; mainly insight, practised in access concentration
quiz.why: "Attending to the in-breath, the out-breath, and the body they depend on realises the aggregate of form." Venerable Miào Jìng: realising the aggregates leans towards insight — practised within access concentration.

quiz.q: In realising dependent origination one finds "body and mind depend on the life faculty." How does Venerable Miào Jìng define it?
options: the force that keeps body and mind joined together
quiz.why: "Having inquired, one truly realises: this body and this mind depend on and are conditioned by the life faculty." Venerable Miào Jìng: the force that holds the physical and the mental together without separating — that is called the life faculty.
